conviction_note: The Q3 guide is $78-85m (mid $81.5m). That midpoint implies revenue falls 1.3% from Q2, although Q3 was the seasonally strong quarter last year (Q2 2025 $84.6m to Q3 2025 $89.6m, +5.9%), and Q2 2026 beat the top of its own guide. I lean to a print at or just above $85m. The Iran war in the Gulf through Q3 and a weaker Q4 margin implied by the full-year 30% net-margin comment offset part of that. There is no usable option chain, so abs_move 5.0 comes from the name's own median reaction (4.5% over 7 real releases), raised a little because a Q4 guide is new. p_up is 54, a proxy-and-inference lean. Findings sum to +1.0; the scaled number is +0.4. The gap comes from the uncertainty that p_up carries.

findings.finding: Q3 is Yalla's seasonally strongest quarter: Q2 2025 $84.6m rose to Q3 2025 $89.6m (+5.9%). The Q3 2026 guide midpoint of $81.5m instead implies a 1.3% fall from Q2 2026's $82.6m. Management's guides have been conservative: Q2 2026 printed $82.6m against a $75-82m guide (above the top), and Q1 2026 printed $79.0m against $75-82m (above the midpoint). Last year's Q2-to-Q3 seasonality applied to Q2 2026 gives about $87m. A print at or above the $85m top is plausible, against a bar the market holds at about the $81.5m midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed above the top of its guide and the stock rose +4.12% the next session (2026-08-18). Q1 2026 printed near the guide midpoint ($79.0m vs $78.5m) and it fell -6.65%. Q4 2025 $83.9m: -8.3%. Q3 2025 $89.6m beat a $86.3m estimate: +1.0%. A mid-range print has been sold; above the top has been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has drifted to $5.43, near its 52-week low and below net cash, with a -3.2% 20-day run-up. That is the price of a name expected to print inside a declining guide. If an above-range print were expected, it would not trade under its cash pile into the release. No dated consensus exists to show analysts sitting above the guide.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 $89.6m comes from a separate document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36033942/yalla-group-limited-announces-unaudited-third-quarter-2025-financial-results, 2025-11-10). The Q2 and Q1 guide-vs-actual figures come from the Q1 2026 release (https://ir.yalla.com/2026-05-18-Yalla-Group-Limited-Announces-Unaudited-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results). Against it: the Q3 guide was set on 2026-08-17 with the July escalation of the Iran war already known, so management may have built that into a below-seasonal range (see the geopolitical finding).

findings.finding: The Iran war that management blamed for the falling paying-user count in Q1 and Q2 ran through Q3 unresolved: escalation in July, Hormuz still nearly shut in late August (Gulf News, 'six months into the Iran war'). MBC and Al Arabia reported Q3 2026 revenue down about 16% on 2026-11-11, citing 'continued geopolitical tensions' hitting advertising. Against that, MBC's consumer subscription arm Shahid grew revenue +10.2% and Jahez GMV grew +45%. Saudi POS spending in the week of 16-22 Aug 2026 was +5.7% YoY (Qoyod on SAMA data). Read net: the war hit advertising budgets, not consumer digital spending, so the transmission to Yalla's virtual-item revenue is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 prints where management blamed geopolitics for fewer paying users (Q4 2025 release, Q1 2026) fell 8.3% and 6.65%. Q2 2026 carried the same explanation but beat the guide and rose 4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The MBC/Al Arabia/Jahez Q3 prints landed on 2026-11-11, after Yalla last spoke on 2026-08-17. But the war itself is public and the Q3 guide was set after the July escalation. If the market feared a worse Q3 than guided, the stock would have broken below its 52-week low ($5.00); it sits 7% above it.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: macro and peer read-through that neither Yalla nor a direct counterparty has confirmed. Positive offset from a broader series: Saudi POS +5.7% YoY week of 16-22 Aug 2026 (https://www.qoyod.com/en/reports/saudi-national-day-spending/). War status: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/12/iran-refutes-trumps-claim-to-control-hormuz-whats-the-latest-in-talks (2026-08-12).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (machine transcript), management said full-year 2026 revenue would be 'broadly in line with 2025' ($341.9m) and full-year GAAP net margin could be around 30%. H1 2026 was $161.6m revenue and $57.7m net income (35.7% margin). Taken literally, H2 needs about $180m, a Q4 near $95-100m if Q3 lands at its midpoint, and H2 net margin of roughly 24-26%. That points to heavy Q4 user-acquisition spend behind the planned Q4 SLG game update. The Q4 guide given tonight is therefore the line that tests the full-year claim. Q4 2025's easy $83.9m comp makes a growth guide likely. But a guide well short of the ~$95m the full-year comment implies, plus an explicit H2 margin step-down, is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Yalla guides one quarter ahead in every release. The Q4 2025 release (Q1 guide $75-82m against $83.9m prior-year) fell -8.3%; the Q2 2026 release (Q3 guide $78-85m, wider and higher than prior ranges) rose +4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The full-year comment sits only in a call transcript with obvious transcription errors (it misstates the Q3 guide as $78-80m), not in the press release, so few have arithmeticked it. If the market believed a $95m+ Q4, the stock would not trade below net cash. If it feared a margin collapse, short interest would not be 1.6% of float.
findings.independence: None. This is one document, and the $341.9m FY2025 figure comes from the Q4 2025 release (https://ir.yalla.com/2026-03-09-Yalla-Group-Limited-Announces-Unaudited-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results). The sign is genuinely two-way: a full-year reiteration would be a positive.

findings.finding: Yalla trades below its cash. Market cap is about $700m at $5.43, against $824.2m of cash, term deposits and short-term investments at 2026-06-30. A $150m repurchase program is authorised (March 2026, 24 months). The company bought $18.0m in Q2 alone at higher prices, and the stock sat at or near its 52-week low through Q3. The release will carry a Q3 repurchase figure, and a step-up or a new return (dividend or tender) is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $150m program was announced with the Q4 2025 release on 2026-03-09 and the stock still fell -8.3% that session. This shareholder base has not paid much for buybacks.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the program is public. The Q3 pace is not, and a pace well above $18m a quarter at sub-cash prices would be new.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with the seasonality finding (different line). Market cap: Fox Business quote $718m at $5.64 on 2026-10-23 (https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=YALA).

findings.finding: Games revenue grew 11.6% YoY to $34.2m in Q2 (41% of revenue). Turbo Match was featured by the Apple App Store across MENA including Saudi Arabia in mid-July. Management also said user-acquisition spend may slow in Q3 ahead of the Q4 SLG update, which should lift Q3 operating margin after Q2 operating income fell to $19.4m from $30.6m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 games growth with an operating-income drop: +4.1%. Margin compression accompanied the Q1 2026 -6.65% (net income $28.4m vs $36.4m).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 margin effect of slower UA was said once on a call and is not reflected in any dated estimate. The market's attention sits on revenue and paying users.
findings.independence: Shares the call transcript with the full-year comment finding. Games growth comes from the press release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/yalla-group-limited-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-544280.shtml). Net of the rest: the chat business (57% of revenue) fell from $48.1m in Q1 to $47.4m in Q2 and drives the total.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A mild positive lean runs against a weak tape: -3.2% over 20 days, near the 52-week low, below net cash. That tape is consistent with a market expecting another in-guide, down-YoY print, so the lean is a contrarian one and p_up is held at 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (narrow proxy loses to a broad series): the geopolitical finding went from -0.5 to -0.2. The ad-revenue read-through from MBC/Al Arabia is offset by the broader Saudi POS +5.7% YoY and Shahid/Jahez consumer growth, now filed inside the same finding.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the full-year comment finding went from -0.5 to -0.4. Its risk sits inside a guidance line whose sign is genuinely two-way, and the transcript is error-prone.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): the seasonality finding stayed at +1.0, because this name bought its last above-the-top print (+4.1%) and sold mid-range ones.
Lesson 7: no crowded short (1.6% of float) and no skew, so no change from positioning.
Lesson 9: the games finding notes the chat business (57% of revenue) is flat to down; the size is left at +0.3.
